definition: Waikato Environment for Knowledge Analysis (Weka) is a collection of machine learning and data analysis free software licensed under the GNU General Public License.
details: It was developed at the University of Waikato, New Zealand, and is the companion software to the book "Data Mining: Practical Machine Learning Tools and Techniques".

explainer.lead: Weka is a free, GPL-licensed collection of machine learning and data analysis software from the University of Waikato, New Zealand. It matters as a teaching and rapid-experimentation toolkit tied to a standard data mining textbook.

tiers.eli5: It is a toolbox of ready-made machine learning tools you can point at a data file to try different methods without writing them yourself.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to prototype classifiers and inspect results quickly, often via its graphical interface. A pitfall is assuming in-memory, desktop-scale experiments will carry over unchanged to large production datasets.
tiers.paperLevel: Not a single algorithm but a software suite implementing many methods. Its capabilities are bounded by the algorithms it ships and by the memory of the machine it runs on.

explainer.example: A student loads a dataset into Weka, runs a decision tree classifier and reads the accuracy and confusion matrix from the output.
